clue.text: Bill on the line expresses agreement

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, and an account is a bill
a cord is a length of string or line

explanation.surface: A bill on the telephone line shows that terms have been agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord is harmony or a settled understanding between parties, a synonym.

clue.text: The English way? Ah, no — but a foreign sort

definitions.text: The English way? Ah, no — but a foreign sort

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and altered, so these letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar form

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a road is the English kind and is told it belongs to another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' is the anagram signal: AHNOBUTA rearranges into the answer, while the whole clue describes it as a road that is not English.
explanation.definitionFit: A German motorway is a kind of road found abroad rather than in England.

clue.text: Wine found in many picnic baskets

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword way of saying many
hampers are lidded baskets for carrying a picnic

explanation.surface: Bottles of wine turn up in plenty of picnic baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' reads like a container, but the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, a sparkling wine.

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for look is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or lewdly

explanation.surface: Glancing upwards makes someone feel giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LEER, written upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or feel the head spinning, a synonym of feeling giddy.

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone points out a nasty wound: look how badly it is cut!
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely means in a harsh or serious way, as badly does in 'badly hurt'.

clue.text: Dinner suits vary in different countries?

definitions.text: Dinner suits vary in different countries?

parts.words: Dinner suits vary in different countries?
parts.note: read 'dinner' as the act of eating and 'suits' as garments such as a monk's robes, so the phrase becomes customs of dining that differ by nation

explanation.definitionFit: Customs at the table differ from one nation to another, which is what dining practices describes.

clue.text: They may be found in a creel, squirming

definitions.text: They may be found in a creel, squirming

indicators.note: found in signals that the letters sit inside the words creel and squirming

explanation.surface: A fisherman's basket holds wriggling catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The run cr(EEL S)quirming gives the answer, and squirming fish in a creel are exactly what the whole clue pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery fish caught by anglers wriggle in a wicker fishing basket.

explanation.surface: Someone departed during a stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a play script the stage direction 'exit' marks an actor going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Exited means went away; in a theatre script an actor who has gone off stage has exited.

explanation.surface: A gambler from the States places a multiple wager.
explanation.walkthrough: In British betting a yankee is a wager of eleven bets on four selections.
explanation.definitionFit: A yankee is a person from the United States, and also a multiple wager placed at a bookmaker.

explanation.surface: Something was located and then reproduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Traced means tracked down or located, and also copied by drawing over a design through thin paper.

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the words lost nail are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse is unhappy because a nail from its shoe has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding is a kind of horse.

clue.text: They have grounds for belonging to the upper classes

definitions.text: They have grounds for belonging to the upper classes

parts.words: They have grounds for belonging to the upper classes
parts.note: grounds looks like reasons or justification, but here it means estates of land owned by a social class

explanation.definitionFit: Families who own country estates form a traditional upper social rank in Britain.

clue.text: Rolls of bread initially well turned

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word bread
turned means the word for well is written backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: Bread rolls are first turned over to bake properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft round bread buns in Britain, so they are a kind of roll.

clue.text: Heavenly food for many a girl

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword way of saying many
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Divine nourishment is provided for lots of young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link here, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Israelites were fed in the wilderness by bread sent from heaven.

parts.note: me is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Something is only a pair of musical tones.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means only or simply, as in 'a mere child'.

clue.text: Tropical bird with head of myna and cry of rook

indicators.note: head of points to the opening letter of the word myna

parts.note: caw is the harsh call of a rook or crow

explanation.surface: An exotic bird has a myna's head and a rook's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America is a tropical bird.

indicators.note: the interior signals that the word for about goes inside the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: There is new intelligence about the inland region of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means new or inexperienced, as in green wood or a green recruit.

explanation.surface: Some places are scattered irregularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Here and there means in scattered places now and then, and also names two spots, this place and that place.

parts.note: the following looks like a list below, but it is the group of supporters of a leader or cause

explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of a cause is one member of its body of followers.

clue.text: Taking tea with Evita requires a third party present

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Eva Peron, nicknamed Evita, was first lady of Argentina

explanation.surface: Having tea with Evita means someone else must be in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an older companion who attends a young couple, an onlooker making three.

clue.text: Workers disturb the bard, in some measure

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands

indicators.note: to disturb is to mess something up, so the words the bard are rearranged

explanation.surface: Labourers interrupt Shakespeare in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturb' turns THEBARD into BREADTH; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The width of a palm, about four inches, is an old unit of measurement.

clue.text: Horse and trap showing sign of neglect

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
a spider's web is a trap for insects

explanation.surface: A horse and carriage look shabby and uncared-for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' suggests the pony-drawn carriage of the surface, but here it is the spider's snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty strands left by spiders build up in rooms nobody has cleaned.

indicators.note: play here means move about freely, so the words lead in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is given the leading role in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a theatre piece, but it signals the anagram of LEADIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a man's name.

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means the word for chatter is turned round

parts.note: to yak is to chatter idly

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that there is nothing worth gossiping over.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is a word of agreement meaning yes or very well.

clue.text: The way part of a match turns into matches

indicators.note: turns means both pieces are read together from the end backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a set is a section of a tennis match

explanation.surface: The way one segment of a contest develops shapes the whole series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses STSET as a whole. Test matches are international cricket or rugby fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: International cricket games are called tests, so the plural means such matches.

explanation.surface: Someone is crafty in the most important respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep means sly or crafty, and 'the deep' is a poetic name for the ocean, as is 'the main'.

indicators.note: provided suggests the letters are prepared or arranged afresh, so the word pass is reordered

explanation.surface: A permit is supplied for visiting health resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' signals a rearrangement of PASS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are towns with mineral springs that people visit for their health.

explanation.surface: Something is discovered to be despicable.
explanation.definitionFit: To base something is to found or ground it on something, and base also means mean and despicable.

indicators.note: about means the word for lashes goes round the word for favourite

parts.note: whips are lashes, as strokes of a whip
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone strikes out at the much-loved hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippets are slim fast racing dogs, so they are a breed of dog.

clue.text: Profession has run rapidly out of control

explanation.surface: A person's line of work has spiralled wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a lifelong occupation, and to career is to rush headlong out of control.

explanation.surface: A dessert that is not heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull's-eye is a lantern with a thick round lens, and a bullseye is a hard British peppermint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull's-eye is an old lantern with a bulging glass lens, and also a striped mint boiled confection.

clue.text: He arranges the grave stone to be assembled about ten

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter for ten
to be assembled suggests putting pieces together in a new form, so the word stone is rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A man lays out a burial plot and has a headstone put together around ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be assembled' turns STONE into SETON, and 'about' puts it round X.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer whose duties include digging graves.
